subject: Closing corridors: legal handshake & evaluation sprint milestones
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <alicia@helixtx.com>, Samir Rao <samir@helixtx.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Closing corridors: legal handshake & evaluation sprint milestones

Hi Alicia / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation I put together a tight mutual action plan and a 3-week evaluation sprint timeline that ties back to the MSA/DPA/order form handoff. The MAP is intentionally prescriptive on the legal checkpoints so we can avoid back-and-forth at signature time.

Key asks from Helix:
- Confirm the technical evaluation window (we proposed Mar 22–Apr 9)
- Confirm acceptance criteria owner(s) and a single list of endpoints we need to validate
- Legal: confirm the redline owner for the MSA/DPA and whether procurement will require a vendor security package in parallel to the DPA

Attached: 2026-03-11-Helix-MAP-v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), 2026-03-11-Eval-Sprint-Roadmap.pdf (detailed sprint), Draft-Order-Form-Helix-Redwood-v0.3.docx (order form stub).

Quick summary of sequencing we recommend (short version):
1) Evaluation sprint (3 weeks) with bi-weekly checkpoints — engineering to confirm pass/fail on test prompts
2) Parallel security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence delivery (Redwood provides SOC2 and audit logs snapshot)
3) Legal review window (MSA first pass) — 5 business days for initial redline from Helix; Redwood will return redline within 3 business days
4) Order form finalized and DocuSign circulation — target signature within 7 business days after legal shape is agreed

We’re aiming to sign and provision dedicated seats by Apr 20. If you need tighter gating or want to accelerate, we can push on priority legal triage with our contracts lead.

Laura / Jordan — looping you for execution: Laura, can you own the security artifact delivery cadence? Jordan, can you act as contract SME and be ready for the initial redline discussion?

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
m: (415) 555-0134

Subject: Re: Closing corridors: legal handshake & evaluation sprint milestones

Thanks Marcus — this is very helpful and well scoped. A few quick notes from our side:

- Evaluation window: the proposed Mar 22–Apr 9 works for engineering. We may need one extra day at the end for stakeholder sign-off (suggest Apr 12 as final acceptance).
- Acceptance criteria: Samir will own the technical checklist; I will own executive acceptance. We’ll send a consolidated list by Friday (2026-03-14).
- Legal: procurement will handle the MSA; I’ve copied procurement. They typically do a 7-business-day first pass, not 5. Can Redwood compress your turnaround?
- Security: we need Redwood’s most recent SOC2 report and a brief on data handling for prefix caching/KV retention — we can start the vendor security review in parallel.

We’ll review the MAP and the draft order form with procurement and come back with a list of redlines and any procurement-specific clauses.

Alicia
VP, Product & Partnerships | Helix Therapeutics
alicia@helixtx.com

Hi Alicia / Samir —

Happy to compress our legal turnaround. If procurement can commit to a 7-business-day first pass, Redwood can commit to returning a counter-redline within 48 business hours for the first two adjudications (MSA and Order Form). For the DPA we will need 3 business days because we coordinate with security on a few clauses.

On SOC2 and evidence: Laura will own the artifact set. Laura — I’ve added Sofia from our security team to help answer any questions about KV/prefix retention and encryption-at-rest details. Alicia / Samir — I’ll coordinate a short legal sync on Monday Mar 22 at 11:00 PT to walk initial procurement asks and set the DocuSign cadence. Please let me know if the time conflicts.

Proposed refined sequencing (with owners and SLA):
- Mar 22–Apr 12: Evaluation sprint (Samir owner) — acceptance signoff by Apr 12 at 17:00 PT
- Mar 22–Apr 5: Parallel vendor security review (Laura owner) — deliver SOC2 and 3 artifacts by Mar 26
- Apr 5–Apr 12: Legal redline window (Procurement first pass Apr 5–Apr 12) — Redwood returns within 2 business days for MSA/order form, 3 business days for DPA
- Apr 13–Apr 20: DocuSign circulation and signature harvest (Jordan owner)

I’m attaching a simple checklist for the DocuSign flow and a short runbook for how we handle mid-redline scope changes (keeps acceptance/timeboxes tight).

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Contracts | Redwood Inference

Alicia / Samir —

Attaching the SOC2 cover letter and the data handling summary for KV/prefix retention. Quick clarifying notes:
- We retain KV cache for up to 24 hours by default; customers can request stricter retention windows as part of Private deployments.
- Encryption-at-rest is AES-256; transit is TLS1.3 and we publish a short KMS rotation policy excerpt in the artifact bundle.
- For the vendor security questionnaire, please send the questionnaire link and I’ll assign a tracker for responses — target turnaround for standard questionnaires is 5 business days.

We’ll be ready to kickoff the evaluation sprint on Mar 22 and plan a 30-minute check-in on Mar 26 to triage any infra items.

Attachments: SOC2-Cover-Helix-Redwood-2026.pdf, KV-Retention-and-KMS-Excerpt.pdf
